article.name: CogZ
article.summary: CogZ is a local-first Rust memory and code-context system for software repositories. It stores observations, rules, and knowledge as Markdown files, indexes them in per-repository SQLite, and combines lexical, vector, and graph retrieval into scoped context packs. This is a source review at the verified master head; this review ran no system, tests, or benchmarks.

article.who_what: The official README presents CogZ as a local-first Rust binary/library and MCP server for repository-specific engineering memory and code-aware context. It describes support for Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, and MCP-compatible agents. The README names balaianu as the repository account, but this review does not infer maintainer identity beyond the official repository attribution.

architecture.text: Canonical records are Markdown files under each repository's .cogz/ directory; .cogz/cogz.db is a disposable SQLite index in WAL mode. FTS5 and sqlite-vec share the database. Tree-sitter creates code entities and structural edges; file entities describe observations, rules, and knowledge.

The file-backed model uses Markdown plus constrained YAML frontmatter with UUID, title, type, status, timestamps, references, and optional provenance/state fields. Code entities use deterministic IDs from normalized source paths and qualified names; generated code relationships are stored in the derived index.

The architecture separates storage/files, embedding, hybrid search, context assembly, indexing, consolidation, hooks, and MCP. A stateless stdio MCP call must name its target repository; the server resolves/caches per-repository state.

behavior.text: Write: create_entity dispatches to observation, rule, or knowledge creation after type-specific validation. MCP writes create a file first, scan for secrets, sync it to SQLite, optionally embed it, and check duplicates/contradictions. The repository documentation describes manual Markdown editing and indexing as another ingestion path.

Update and correction: knowledge is the only file-backed type with in-place content edits; update_knowledge reads the existing item, writes the revised file, syncs only that file, restores the previous content if sync fails, then re-embeds and records an event. Observations are append-only for content; rules are changed by superseding and creating a new rule. verify re-stamps code provenance and is an attestation, not a truth check.

Delete and retention: rejected or superseded observations can be explicitly pruned after the configured retention age. Pruning empties the canonical file and removes its FTS entry and embedding while preserving graph edges; the tombstone remains until bounded-retention cleanup removes old tombstones. Active/stale observations and rules/knowledge are not pruned by this path. This is lifecycle deletion, not proof of erasure from backups, Git history, or external copies.

Retrieval: search combines FTS5, separate code/knowledge vector indexes, graph-first retrieval and post-fusion graph expansion using reciprocal-rank fusion and ranking adjustments. Context assembly orders rules and other sections, removes duplicates, compresses the tail, fits a token budget, and lists dropped entities as pointers. Search responses can carry graph paths and answer-coverage signals.

Scope isolation: data and the SQLite index are per checkout/repository, and the MCP server requires an explicit repo argument for each tool call. The reviewed design does not describe user/tenant authorization within one repository database; host permissions and selecting the correct repository remain deployment responsibilities.

Provenance and evidence: file frontmatter can record source, supporting observations, references, derived-from relationships, and verified code hashes. Search exposes curated graph paths and provenance-related ranking; domain events and delivery/access tracking provide operational traces. These mechanisms preserve lineage and context, but do not guarantee claim-level citations or that a generated answer is supported by its sources.

Efficiency and observability: local storage avoids a separate database service, FTS works without models, and model inference can be optional/lazy. Search uses batched graph/embedding operations; context packs enforce a token budget. CLI status/doctor, usage counters, domain events, and structured logs expose operational state. The README's performance/evaluation numbers are upstream-reported claims and are not measurements from this review.

metrics.evidence: Search has a configurable answer-coverage silence gate and reports coverage signals, but this task ran no adjudicated answerable/unanswerable queries.
Source paths include knowledge updates and code-drift demotion; no correction probes or stale-retrieval workload was run.
The prune path tombstones content and removes FTS/vector data while preserving edges; no post-prune or replica/history leakage check was performed.
Per-repository databases and explicit repo parameters are visible in source/docs; no cross-repository or hostile caller isolation workload was run.
Lineage, graph paths, and answer-coverage signals exist, but no generated answer was adjudicated for claim support or citation correctness.
No latency timings or distributions were collected in this review.
No timed write-then-correct-recall workload was run.
No token/provider usage or cost accounting was performed.
The local file/index architecture is documented, but no corpus size or per-record storage measurement was collected.

limits.text: This review inspected selected official README/design docs and current pinned write, update, and pruning implementations. It does not establish behavior for every MCP tool, hook, platform, model combination, error path, or repository configuration.

Search documentation reports benchmark findings and known precision/negative-query limitations, but those are upstream reports rather than measurements reproduced in this review. No CogZ runtime, benchmark, or test was run.

The coverage-based silence gate cannot establish semantic answerability for all queries; the docs describe residual false opens and false silences. Graph expansion can add related but irrelevant items, and code/knowledge embeddings use incompatible models.

File-backed storage and per-repository databases provide a local boundary, but no in-database tenant authorization was established by this source review. Pruning does not establish complete deletion from Git history, backups, or consumer copies.

benchmark.note: No CogZ runtime, benchmark, or tests were run for this assessment. Source observations and upstream README benchmark claims are not project benchmark results.
